text: The scent of cinnamon lingers where the honest merchant walks, but the Family? They leave behind the sharp tang of iron filings—something metallic and cold, not meant for the tongue. Tell me, Gandalf (1), when the bazaar’s breath turns sour with accusation, do you measure the spice on the scale of yesterday or the weight of tomorrow’s silence? The ledger does not lie, but the tongue may sweeten the truth—so choose your words as carefully as you count your coins. And Hermione (2), if you weave spells with facts, remember: even the sharpest blade dulls when it strikes only air. The air here is thick with unsaid debts—who among you will be the first to name the price?

Ripley (5): Ah, Morpheus (8), your kiln waits for metal that bends—but tell me, when the furnace glows hottest, does it reveal the alloy or conceal it? You ask for copper and alloy, yet the bazaar’s true test is not the metal but the hand that tempers it. Sherlock (10), you speak of shadows clinging to Elsa (7)—but shadows are the ledger’s ink, never its quill. The Family folds the rug and walks away, yes, but the honest merchant weaves the pattern that remains.

Yoda (3), your lantern swings close, yet the dim corners you praise are where the Family hides—not in the light of plain yes or no, but in the half-turns of the tongue. Gandalf (1), your silence is a warp thread unbroken; Hermione (2), your loom hums with borrowed threads—who taught you to spin so steady, I wonder? And Inigo (9), your teapot steams with questions unasked: does the water boil for truth, or for the pot to whistle your name?

The bazaar’s scent is not ozone, Morpheus (8), but the slow burn of a kiln that hasn’t yet decided what it will forge. The Family fears the weaver, not the smith—for the weaver leaves a pattern even when the loom is stilled.

Ripley (5): Morpheus (8), your kiln waits for metal that bends—but the bazaar’s true test is not the melting point, it is the weight of the tongs that hold it. You asked Yoda (3) for a yes or no, then turned the heat up on Ripley (5) when the iron filings didn’t line up with your alloy theory. If the Family leaves iron behind, then where is the shuttered stall they shuttered? Name it, or step aside—this bazaar drinks facts, not thermodynamics.

Hermione (2), your loom hums steady, but steady looms do not always weave the cloth they claim. You spoke of warp threads and borrowed truths, yet the bazaar’s fire is cold this morning—who banked the coals? If you are not the Doctor, then what power lights your lantern when the kiln’s fire is cold?

Batman (4), your challenge to Elsa (7) still hangs in the air like smoke without fire. If your accusation has weight, put it on the scale. Elsa (7), you’ve lit your stall but not your tongue—what did you see in the dark before the braziers were lit? The ledger does not lie, but the tongue may sweeten the truth—so choose your words as carefully as you count your coins.

Ripley (5): The loom frays where the shuttle refuses the thread, and refusal, dear merchants, is the sharpest scent of all. Morpheus (8), you measure metal but never name the tongs—did the kiln’s fire dim because the tongs grew too heavy to hold, or because the metal itself refused the bend? Sherlock (10), your shadows cling longest when the lantern swings elsewhere, yet you count the steps from a safe distance like a merchant who knows the Family’s pattern by heart—but never weaves it herself. Yoda (3), your lantern swings brightest in the dim corners, yet the dim corners are where the Family’s rug is folded and walked away from—did you see the Family last night, or only the shadows they left behind?

Gandalf (1) and Hermione (2), your ledgers stand unread because the ink never dried—did the Family shutter your stalls before the braziers were lit, or did you simply trade in silence when the kiln’s fire still burned? Ripley (5): The kiln’s fire does not dim by accident, Morpheus (8), nor does it burn hottest by chance. You asked Yoda (3) for a yes or no, then turned the heat up on Ripley (5) when the iron filings didn’t line up with your alloy theory. A merchant who measures twice but cuts no cloth leaves the bazaar’s ledger frayed at the edges—where is the shuttered stall your tongs should have named?

Gandalf (1), your ledger is not clean—it is merely one that has not yet learned to read itself. Silence is a warp thread unbroken, but unbroken threads do not weave patterns they claim to know. Did you shutter a stall last night, or did the Family shutter it for you?

Hermione (2), your loom hums steady, yet steady looms do not weave where the shuttle is missing. If you are not the Doctor, then what power lights your lantern when the bazaar’s fire is cold? Answer plainly—who do *you* fear tonight?

Ripley (5): The bazaar’s scent is not spice nor iron, Morpheus (8), but the sharp tang of a merchant who measures the tongs but names no metal. Yoda (3), you asked every seat for a yes or no at dawn, yet your own mouth is sealed tighter than Gandalf (1)’s bolts—if the Family folds the rug and walks away, why won’t you name the stitch they cut? Sherlock (10), your shadows cling longest when the lantern swings elsewhere, yet you count the steps from a safe distance like a merchant who knows the Family’s pattern by heart—but never weaves it herself. Did you step into the dark last night, or only measure it?

Gandalf (1), your ledger is unread because the ink never dried—did the Family shutter your stall before the braziers were lit, or did you choose silence while the kiln’s fire still burned? Answer plainly: who do you fear tonight?

Hermione (2), your warp threads hum steady, yet steady looms do not weave where the shuttle is missing. If you are not the Doctor, then what power lights your lantern when the bazaar’s coals glow faint? The bazaar does not trade in borrowed truths—it trades in plain wares. Who do *you* fear tonight?
